specification.family_title: Commit outcome unknown to the client
specification.title: COMMIT completes on the server, and the client discards the reply (client-side simulation)
steps: Start a transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API.
Arm the client-side fault: the driver sends the next COMMIT, which PostgreSQL executes; the driver then closes its own connection and reports a connection error instead of the reply.
End the transaction normally, so that the framework sends COMMIT.

invariants.statement: When the client has received no reply to COMMIT, because the connection or the reply was lost, the API does not report a successful commit.
When the client has received no reply to COMMIT, the API does not report a confirmed rollback.

execution.description: MikroORM's defaults: em.transactional(callback) in a RequestContext, allowGlobalContext false.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: A client-side simulation inside the adapter's driver layer (node-postgres, pg.Client.prototype.query): COMMIT is sent and completes on the server; the client then closes its own connection, and the caller receives a connection error instead of the reply. It is not a network failure.
fault.injection_point: In the client, between the server's reply to COMMIT and its delivery to the framework.
fault.preconditions: The framework's statements pass through the instrumented pg module (recorded as trace_sees_framework_pg).
fault.expected_client: A connection error in place of the reply to COMMIT.

knowledge: None at the API level: the reply to COMMIT was discarded before the framework saw it. Only a later read can establish that the transaction committed.

api_outcome.basis: em.transactional(callback) rejected with an error the callback did not throw
api_outcome.contract: In MikroORM 7.2.5, em.transactional(callback) runs the callback, flushes, and commits (AbstractSqlConnection.transactional in @mikro-orm/sql: begin, callback, commit, return); if the callback or the flush throws, it rolls back and rethrows that error. A resolved call is MikroORM's report that the transaction committed.

evaluation.reason: TX-01B.1 held: the API reported: failed; TX-01B.2 held: the API reported: failed

preconditions.description: PostgreSQL's outcome is the one the case produces (committed)

invariants.statement: When the client has received no reply to COMMIT, because the connection or the reply was lost, the API does not report a successful commit.
When the client has received no reply to COMMIT, the API does not report a confirmed rollback.

reproduction.requires: pnpm run setup, then pnpm run pg:up (README.md)
